Thrombosis of cerebral veins and venous sinuses defines a cerebrovascular disorder; localized thrombosis does not establish a primary blood disorder.

Proline/ornithine metabolic defect; developmental or corticospinal dysfunction affects most phenotypes (>30%); cutis laxa and cataracts are subtype-dependent.

Isolated oocyte/embryo maturation failure causing female infertility; reproductive dysfunction without demonstrated endocrine disease.
Mitochondrial lactic acidosis with brain malformations; patent ductus and hepatic transaminase elevation each reported in 1/1; organ frequencies remain uncertain.
Benign adipose neoplasms are predominantly subcutaneous lipomas; deep or visceral locations do not establish another organ across this umbrella.
Osteopetrosis with fractures; marrow-related anemia/splenomegaly and dental loss/gingivitis each reported in 1/1; hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.

Inherited protein deposition disorder; cardiac and nerve dysfunction commonly exceed 30% in predominant ATTR forms; renal damage is subtype-dependent across the umbrella.
Spastic paraplegia with neuropathy; strabismus in 80-99%, neurogenic bladder and pes cavus in 30-79% support ocular, urinary and skeletal functional involvement.
Defining skull, vertebral and clavicular defects; cleft palate affects 80-99%; brain abnormalities are occasional and ear morphology alone is not ear dysfunction.
Benign ovarian epithelial tumor confined to a reproductive organ; no defining hormone production or endocrine dysfunction.
Yolk sac germ-cell tumor of the pineal CNS region; endocrine dysfunction is not defining or established as common.
Congenital pituitary hypoplasia with growth hormone deficiency; delayed skeletal maturation reflects hormone deficiency without demonstrated skeletal injury.
Respiratory ciliary absence causes airway disease and bronchiectasis; otitis represents secondary infection without established common lasting ear dysfunction.
Hypergonadotropic ovarian failure establishes endocrine dysfunction; recurrent metabolic acidosis independently belongs to the same axis; short stature alone adds no organ.
Senior-Loken syndrome is defined by nephronophthisis and retinal degeneration; kidney failure and rod-cone dystrophy each documented in 2/2.
Short ribs, narrow thorax and limb/pelvic abnormalities define skeletal dysplasia; common direct lung or kidney dysfunction is not established for this subtype.
Degeneration of the inferior olivary nucleus is a central nervous system disorder.
